result:
**Verdict: FAIL, on one point.** The add-on rewrites `package.json` with HTML-escaped strings, so it doesn't fully keep the app's handwritten configuration. Everything else in the goal holds.

## What I ran
- `go test ./internal/tailwind/ -count=1`: `ok … 0.152s`, all tests pass.
- **Whether the tests catch breakage:** I broke the code eight ways, one at a time. Every break made a test fail:
  - Gimbal's fixed `../**/*.go` path instead of one worked out from the stylesheet
  - exclusion measured from `web/src` instead of the frontend root
  - always adding `@source not` again
  - always adding the layout import again
  - always reinstalling
  - no check for Tailwind 3 CSS
  - no check for old dependency versions
  - treating CSS comments as real setup
- I restored `plugin.go` and checked it matches the original (sha `28e2f557…`).
- `go build ./cmd/skgo` and `go vet ./internal/tailwind ./cmd/skgo` both pass.

## Assessment against the goal
- **Vite/CSS setup via vp:** it adds `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.3 inside VitePlus's existing `lazyPlugins(() => [...])`, adds `@import "tailwindcss"` to the CSS, and imports the stylesheet from the root layout. Installation goes through `vp install`, the same shape as upstream `sv add tailwindcss`.
- **Go excluded, scope from the stylesheet:** the `@source not` path is computed relative to the actual stylesheet, pointing at the frontend root. Both fixtures got `../../**/*.go`. The scanner check (`fresh-scan.json`) shows 4 Go files scanned before and 0 after, including `web/development.go` and `src/routes/page.server.go`, with the same 20 frontend files both times. The add-on sets no Vite watch or ignore rules.
- **Dev behaviour:** the parent's browser checks cover what the proof asks for. In both apps the document never reloaded, and the draft and the second view survived separate Go edits at the frontend root and beside a route, with `ROOT_TWO_350` and `ROUTE_TWO_350` showing up. The dev logs agree: Go edits produce rebuilds followed by `__data.json` refetches, and the CSS/Svelte edits produce `(client) hmr update`, not a client full reload. The utility class and CSS changes showed up as computed style changes.
- **Repeat runs and conflicts:** a second run reports no changed paths in both live apps and in the tests. Conflicts are rejected before anything is written, and a cancelled run reports no changes.

## Finding: the add-on escapes `&`, `<` and `>` in `package.json`
`internal/tailwind/plugin.go:182-191` re-encodes `package.json` with `json.Marshal`/`MarshalIndent`, and Go escapes `&`, `<` and `>` by default. Every `&&` in the app's scripts becomes `\u0026\u0026`.

- **In a fresh app:** the live fixture now contains `"preview": "cd .. \u0026\u0026 just serve"`. That's the line `skgo new` wrote as `&&`, so the add-on breaks something skgo itself generated. See `ephemeral/tailwind-live/fresh/web/package.json`.
- **In an existing app:** I wrote a scratch test in `internal/tailwind` (since deleted) using the package's `fixture` helper with this authored file:
  ```json
  {"name":"existing-app", ..., "scripts":{"check":"svelte-kit sync && svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json"}, "devDependencies":{"vite-plus":"catalog:"}}
  ```
  After `Apply`, `scripts.check` reads `"svelte-kit sync \u0026\u0026 svelte-check …"` and the indentation changes from tabs to two spaces.

The JSON still means the same thing, but the handwritten file is visibly changed. The two existing `package.json` writers turn this escaping off with `SetEscapeHTML(false)` (`internal/newapp/newapp.go:818`, `internal/update/frontend.go:125`); the add-on doesn't. The current tests only check dependency values in `package.json`, so they can't catch this. Key reordering isn't part of the finding, because `skgo new` already writes `package.json` in alphabetical key order.

## Housekeeping
I made no implementation changes and no commits, and removed my scratch test and backup. Two new files appeared during my run, `03-tailwind-live.log` and `03-tailwind-scan.json`, which came from parallel work. I left the parent's fixtures and the two dev servers (PIDs 50419 and 51491) running. The fix only touches `package.json` formatting, so the browser proof stands, but `03-live-apps.md` says to delete `ephemeral/tailwind-live/` once qualification is finished.
